title: Quarterly customer narrative – Cedarline Financial
body:
Purpose: Draft narrative and slide-level speaker notes for the upcoming Cedarline Financial quarterly business review. Focus: usage health, cost optimization wins, roadmap alignment for private deployment option, and early renewal positioning.

Meeting objectives:
- Reaffirm value delivered this quarter (latency, cost, reliability improvements).
- Surface product roadmap items most relevant to Cedarline (on-prem connector, KMS integration timeline).
- Address outstanding performance tickets and present concrete remediation timeline.
- Establish renewal cadence and proposed commercial terms for June 2026 renewal.

Audience: Cedarline executive sponsors (SVP Product: Laura Meyers), Head of Engineering (Alex Rivera), Head of ML Ops (Dr. Anika Bose), procurement lead (Tom Holt). Internal presenters: Maya Chen (CS), Dmitri Volkov (Solutions Eng), Priya Patel (Account Exec).

Suggested agenda & slide-level notes:
1) Intro & agenda (2 min)
- Note: quick context-setting, confirm time goals, highlight positive momentum.

2) High-level health snapshot (3 slides, 5 min)
- Slide: Key metrics at-a-glance (Uptime, p95 latency, token throughput, monthly spend vs. forecast).
- Speaker note: Lead with improvements: p95 down 18% since Sep after runtime tuning; forecast spend within 7% of committed baseline. Call out the two burst events and how fallbacks held.

3) Usage patterns & cost drivers (2 slides, 6 min)
- Slide: Workload breakdown (chat vs batch embeddings vs reranking).
- Speaker note: Show that embeddings surged 42% MoM due to search pilot; propose batching/quantization adjustments in Optimize to reduce unit cost by projected 24%.

4) Reliability incidents & resolution timeline (1 slide, 4 min)
- Slide: Incident timeline and RCA summary for last two Sev2 events.
- Speaker note: Dmitri to explain fix applied, remaining monitoring steps, and SLO commitments. Emphasize rollback and canary policies now in place.

5) Product roadmap alignment: Private + Compliance features (3 slides, 8 min)
- Slide: Private deployment roadmap and expected milestones (VPC control plane GA Q3, HSM integration prototype Q4).
- Speaker note: Position private deployment as the next step for regulated workloads; ask about Cedarline’s timeline for a pilot.

6) Customer success case study (1 slide, 4 min)
- Slide: Business outcome story — assisted underwriting pilot reduced manual review time by 32%.
- Speaker note: Tie outcome to adoption: ask Alex about scaling to additional underwriting flows.

7) Renewal conversation & commercial proposal (1 slide, 6 min)
- Slide: Renewal timeline options and recommended commercial structure (18-month rolling committed capacity with burst credits).
- Speaker note: Priya to lead: propose an anchor renewal offer with a 10% volume discount conditioned on a June signature, plus a scoped Pilot for private deployment at a fixed engineering effort cap.

8) Risks & mitigations (1 slide, 3 min)
- Slide: Top 3 risks (embedding cost growth, private deployment timeline misalignment, procurement delays) and mitigations (Optimize workshop, dedicated SE for pilot, procurement checklist).

9) Action items & next steps (1 slide, 2 min)
- Slide: Clear next steps, owners, due dates.
- Speaker note: Confirm meeting cadence for renewal negotiations (weekly sync) and technical pilot kickoff date.

Tailored talking points (short bullets for each persona):
- For Laura Meyers (SVP Product): Focus on business outcomes and time-to-market; show reduction in mean review cycle and how Redwood features enable faster product launches. Ask: what KPIs would justify expansion?
- For Alex Rivera (Head of Eng): Focus on latency SLOs, runtime tuning wins, and private deployment readiness. Ask: acceptable maintenance window for pilot; concerns about integration with internal CI.
- For Dr. Anika Bose (Head of ML Ops): Emphasize KV cache hit improvements, quantization tradeoffs, and model versioning controls in Console. Ask: which workloads must remain float32?
- For Tom Holt (Procurement): Focus on predictable spend and contractual SLAs. Ask: preferred contracting cadence and legal points on data residency.

Renewal script (concise):
- Opening: Thank you for partnership, quick recap of delivered outcomes this quarter.
- Transition: We’d like to align on an opportunity to renew early to secure predictable capacity and the pilot slot for your private deployment.
- Ask: Commit to an 18-month reserved commitment at X units/month with burst credits; in exchange Redwood will provide a scoped private-deploy pilot and a joint success plan.
- Close: Request decision timeline and confirm procurement contacts.

Proposed commercial levers (internal note):
- Anchor: 18-month reserved capacity with 10% discount.
- Upside: Add-on burst credits at reduced rate for first 3 months post-renewal.
- Services: 60 engineering hours included for private pilot; additional hours billable at a pre-agreed rate.

Risks observed this quarter (detailed):
- Embeddings cost growth driven by broad retrieval experiments without caching.
- Two latency spikes tied to unusually long sequences—mitigated with sequence truncation heuristics but needs model-side testing.
- Procurement schedule: Cedarline’s legal team typically takes 6–8 weeks from commercial term agreement.

Mitigations and asks for Cedarline:
- Schedule Optimize workshop in next 2 weeks to implement batching and prefix caching. (Owner: Dmitri)
- Agree to pilot private deployment scope and sign MOU by 2026-04-15 to secure Q3 pilot slot. (Owner: Maya/Priya)
- Provide procurement gatekeeper contact to accelerate contract review. (Owner: Priya)

Appendix: Data sources and backup slides (for internal prep)
- Billing export: last 90 days (S3 path) — used for spend delta analysis.
- Incident tickets: CS-2982, SRE-1471 — summarised in backup slide.
- Optimize recommendation deck (attached) with expected savings breakdown.

Desired outcome from this QBR:
1) Secure early renewal commitment path and procurement timeline.
2) Lock private deployment pilot scope and kickoff date.
3) Schedule Optimize implementation and define measurable success metrics (target: 20% unit cost reduction within 8 weeks).

Notes to self / open questions to resolve ahead of meeting:
- Confirm exact token pricing to use for the commercial slide (Priya).
- Get latest latency percentiles from SRE dashboard (Dmitri).
- Validate legal redlines for data residency clause (Samir).

Meeting prep checklist (2 days ahead):
- Dry run with internal presenters (30 min).
- Upload finalized slides to shared folder; include appendix with metric exports.
- Send pre-read to Cedarline 48 hours before meeting.

Tone guidance: keep it business-outcome-driven and direct. Avoid deep technical dive unless asked — have backup technical slides ready.

Revision history: initial draft 2025-11-12 by Maya Chen; updated 2026-03-01 with revised renewal proposal and pilot timing.
